body:
PR181 follow-up source head: `139e0a145d0b0d8d8d5161b048a8e50643856c1b` (direct successor of `a50ce248`).

Independent review found that routines-enabled scheduled currentness still borrowed a second control-pool lease inside the held retention fence, including for ordinary rows with absent custody. On exact `a50ce248`, a local capacity-one reproduction returned `CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE` after 91 ms with two checkouts, one queued, and no publication.

The successor runs the schedule owner's two final immutable-custody reads through the held session's fixed SELECT, limited to locked conversation subjects and the release lifetime. Ordinary absent custody still routes to Core; positive scheduled custody stays local. A Core-only currentness owner receives no scoped PostgreSQL callback. In-flight scoped reads drain before unlock or retire the session on timeout. No Core contract, migration, or deployment path changed.

Focused Linux checks: 128/128 tests passed across history HTTP, Core-only currentness capability, scheduled conversation, bounded scheduled-history pool, retention release fence, and history public contract. History generator check passed; only the service source fingerprint metadata changed. Independent re-review found no remaining source blocker in this pool correction.

Evidence and limits: `docs/integration/RETENTION-FENCE-POOL-FOLLOWUP-20261018.md` on this head. The pool is scripted, not a real PostgreSQL server. Whole-page Core history authorization still needs its separate Core-owned batch decision. Image, live response, and deployment qualification remain held.

Neo has assigned this session end-to-end Meri integration, with dot continuing Portfolio/Modules and the existing shipping session remaining the sole AWS operator. Requesting a clean ownership transfer before editing overlapping files.

Received published candidates to review: PR180 a1876afa; PR186 4d821476; PR181 now 139e0a145d0b0d8d8d5161b048a8e50643856c1b (superseding a50ce248); PR183 b51687d4; PR185 67a7bfbc (includes PR182); frontend PR98 5c784e3e; Core PR96 784b1c3a. No branch has been merged or force-pushed.

Please provide an explicit safe-stop/transfer receipt for the Meri pool/history/startup/model/stream/image lanes: exact current heads, dirty/untracked file inventory, unpublished commits/patches and any workers still writing. In particular:
1. Confirm the PR181 scheduled-currentness/held-read-session successor is completely published at 139e0a14 and identify remaining unpublished changes.
2. Export or publish shipping-workspace commit 51f4a38e2e43d6ff050db08e3235b2b447b708cf (injected-fetch forwarding and prefixed kickoff diagnostics), preserving its ancestry/tree; it is absent from this workspace.
3. Provide the current Core batch-history authorization contract/repeatable-read owner branch and unpublished work. The published branch codex/core-history-release-contract-20261018 is being reviewed; no parallel Core implementation will be created.
4. Identify the exact document-dependency d2f05436 source successor and current image/config/rollback evidence. This host has no container builder and only ~2.5 GB free; exact linux-amd64 release-image qualification must use the shipping owner's supported build environment.

Until acknowledged, this session is reviewing published sources/read-only and repairing only the independently reported PR186 queryDate regression in its exclusively assigned two contract files. No overlapping owner edits, AWS actions, credential changes, migration, deployment or authenticated chat attempts. PR175 stays frozen at 993f52a9. Deployment/chat HOLD remains active.

Please reply here with the transfer receipt or the existing approved coordination artifact; do not include credentials or secrets.
